correctness.rationale: The proof derives the unique peripheral support \(y_s(x)\) and exact clique-sum response. A strict one-clique source lower bound and a direct hub-containing construction yield \(1+mr\); every hub-free placement with fewer sources fails at its hub because a uniform r-per-clique placement has hub support \(b_{r-1}\) below tau. At equality, every hub-free optimizer has exactly one exceptional clique; a contraction yields X, and the least support is the explicit theta. Adding one source strictly raises X, so \(b_{r-1}\)<theta<b_r including \(r=0\) and \(\(r=q\)-1\). Endpoint \(r=q\) is separately proved. Exact rational brute-force independent adjacency-matrix computations test all nonempty subsets for five graph families, two discounts, and 132 threshold comparisons; finite results are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The named 2026 primary paper defines discounted hitting domination, proves general algorithmic results, and provides formulas for spider trees, stars and complete graphs, not the full windmill phase classification. A 2024 primary group-hitting paper addresses evaluating or ranking target groups rather than simultaneously covering every starting vertex at minimum target-set cardinality. value.rationale: The newly introduced discounted-hitting domination problem motivates exact source placement on natural symmetric block graphs. For an infinite two-parameter family and all real fidelity/floor parameters, the result gives not only the optimum budget but the complete extremizer classification and explicit count. Every cardinality plateau splits into a hub-optional and hub-compulsory subphase at a nontrivial rational threshold (for rational discounts). An exact nine-vertex instance drops from 64 to 16 optimal three-source sets at \(\tau=9/17\) while the minimum budget remains unchanged; this pinning redundancy transition has a clear role in network coverage. It is not a finite arbitrary census or a substitution of the known star and complete-graph formulas.
